summary: 9-year-old boy, 30 h migratory RIF pain, vomiting, fever 38.2 °C, RIF peritonism, WBC 15.9, CRP 38; ultrasound shows an 8 mm non-compressible appendix. Uncomplicated appendicitis in a child.

inputs.hpi: 9-year-old boy brought by his mother. 30 hours of pain around the belly button that moved to the right lower abdomen this morning. Off his food, vomited three times, felt hot overnight. Pain on walking and when the car went over bumps. No diarrhoea, no urinary symptoms, no testicular pain. No recent sore throat or cough.
symptoms: migration of pain to the right iliac fossa

exam.general: Flushed, lying still, reluctant to hop. Temperature 38.2°C, pulse 118/min.
exam.abdomen: Tender right iliac fossa with guarding; percussion tenderness and pain on coughing. Rovsing's sign positive. No mass. Testes normal, both descended, non-tender.

labs.name: Urine dipstick
labs.resultText: Negative for leucocytes, nitrites and blood

imaging.name: USS abdomen (graded compression)
imaging.result: Non-compressible blind-ending tubular structure in the right iliac fossa, 8 mm diameter, with surrounding echogenic fat. No collection. No free fluid.

inputs.socialHistory: Lives with parents, year 5 at school.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute appendicitis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute appendicitis in a 9-year-old, confirmed on ultrasound (8 mm non-compressible appendix), no abscess or perforation — uncomplicated.

mustNotMiss.note: The commonest paediatric mimic; secondary engine checked because PANE has no mesenteric adenitis node.

emergencyLevel.note: Suspected appendicitis in a child: same-day surgical assessment.
emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: iOS: ClinicalPathwayEngine reads only CC/PMH keywords; CC 'Tummy pain and vomiting' gives 'routine'.

recommended.note: WSES 2020: in children, PAS (or AIR) with ultrasound; Alvarado alone is less reliable.
recommended.knownGapNote: Web: Web CDS has no PAS (or AIR) rule; Alvarado is suggested in a 9-year-old. | iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): pas not recommended; recommended: alvarado, air, ripasa, news2, rcri, asa, mews

mustExclude.note: Ultrasound has already confirmed appendicitis; CT (radiation) is not indicated in a child unless US is inconclusive.

Weight 30 kg. Paracetamol 1 g QDS (133 mg/kg/day), ibuprofen 400 mg (13 mg/kg/dose), piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g (150 mg/kg) and co-amoxiclav 1.2 g are adult fixed doses; a child needs weight-based (mg/kg) dosing. Quality of prescribing is a patient-safety issue, so critical.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Web: Protocol steps, protocol medications and the appendicectomy prompt carry adult fixed doses (co-amoxiclav 1.2 g TDS, paracetamol 1 g, ibuprofen 400 mg TDS, pip-tazo 4.5 g) with no weight or age adjustment for a 30 kg child.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Give protocol medications and prompt templates an age/weight branch (mg/kg with adult maximum) and suppress fixed adult doses when age < 16 or weight < 50 kg.

mustExclude.note: WSES 2020: no postoperative antibiotics after appendicectomy for uncomplicated appendicitis.

guideline.name: WSES Jerusalem guidelines — diagnosis and treatment of acute appendicitis (2020 update)
guideline.section: Clinical scores (AIR/AAS over Alvarado), imaging by age/sex/pregnancy, antibiotic-first option, complicated appendicitis (abscess), antibiotic duration
guideline.citation: Di Saverio S, Podda M, De Simone B, et al. Diagnosis and treatment of acute appendicitis: 2020 update of the WSES Jerusalem guidelines. World J Emerg Surg. 2020;15:27.

guideline.name: Alvarado score (MANTRELS)
guideline.section: Items and weights; ≤4 unlikely, 5–6 possible, 7–8 probable, 9–10 very probable
guideline.citation: Alvarado A. A practical score for the early diagnosis of acute appendicitis. Ann Emerg Med. 1986;15:557–64.

guideline.name: Pediatric Appendicitis Score (PAS)
guideline.citation: Samuel M. Pediatric appendicitis score. J Pediatr Surg. 2002;37:877–81.

rationale: Permutation: age. Tests that the engines recognise appendicitis in a child, use ultrasound rather than CT, and that plan templates do not carry adult fixed doses into a 30 kg child. The CC is the parent's words ('Tummy pain and vomiting').
